source.title: Comparing the information content of probabilistic representation spaces
source.authors: Kieran A. Murphy; Sam Dillavou; Danielle S. Bassett

record.tranche_reason: The study measures shared information in probabilistic representation spaces across independently trained models, using NMI and VI rather than the original studies' methods. Its results bear on convergence across seeds and on sensitivity to the similarity measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports channel-level similarity across model ensembles and full-latent-space similarity across training runs. Model-fusion results are excluded as evidence of naturally occurring convergence because the synthesis space is explicitly optimized to resemble the ensemble. Synthetic-space comparisons of metrics are also excluded as findings about convergence: they compare measurement methods, not independently trained models.
record.test_reason: The study uses new information-theoretic measures (generalized NMI and VI) to compare probabilistic latent spaces. It applies them to ensembles of VAE and InfoGAN models trained from different random seeds, so it measures whether seed-repeat models learn the same information fragments (V3). It also compares fragments across disentanglement methods on cars3d (V5) and contrasts NMI with VI on the same channel pairs (V6). Model fusion and the synthetic-space metric comparison are not evidence of naturally arising convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present this mainly as a methods paper: generalized NMI and VI, plus a Bhattacharyya fingerprint estimator, for comparing probabilistic spaces. Applying them, they find consistently recurring information fragments in VAE and InfoGAN seed ensemble channels, especially under strong regularization, and recognizable fragments across methods. Full latent-space information is largely consistent across seeds, with a transient drop during training. They also show the measures enable model fusion, and argue that channel-level inspection beats model-level or ground-truth-factor metrics for evaluating disentanglement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses information-theoretic comparisons of probabilistic latent spaces, with NMI and VI estimated using Monte Carlo or Bhattacharyya fingerprints; it does not reproduce the original studies' measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Channel-level consistency varies with dataset and regularization/hyperparameter. Full-space consistency varies by method and hyperparameter on smallnorb and changes during training. NMI and VI can distinguish channel relationships differently.

fits_no_version.finding: On nine synthetic probabilistic spaces, the similarity measures disagree: linear CKA and stochastic shape metrics miss similarities that NMI, VI and Bhattacharyya-based CKA detect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The choice of similarity measure changes which representation spaces are judged similar (shown on synthetic, not trained, spaces).

record.problems: The central channel-consistency results are mostly qualitative descriptions of figures, without exact similarity values in the text. The experiments focus on relatively low-dimensional VAE and InfoGAN latent spaces; the paper notes that mutual-information estimation may be challenging at higher dimensions. No controls are reported for the convergence findings.
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing claim-relevant rows were omitted.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no large models of different architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
Neurons and hidden-layer units are not tested, only probabilistic latent channels and full latent spaces of small VAE/GAN models.
No mapping, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment between trained models. Model fusion optimizes a new space toward the ensemble and is not a test.
No neurons, SAE features or circuits. Cross-method comparison is limited to three VAE variants on cars3d.
No out-of-distribution inputs, and no sweep of measure settings such as neighbour count. Only NMI and VI are compared on trained models.
No test of whether shared data or objectives explain alignment, and no plateau with scale. Incompleteness across seeds is recorded under V3.

missing.what: Channel-consistency analysis on 50 MNIST β-VAEs (β=8) and fashion-mnist (β=4), with latent traversals showing consistent groupings
β sweeps (1 to 16) for dsprites and smallnorb β-VAE channel similarity under NMI and VI; the text says block-diagonal structure emerges with increasing β
For full latent spaces, VI was more revealing of heterogeneity than NMI, which becomes unreliable when transmitted information is small (a metric-dependence statement)

record.verdict_notes: All rows now link only to V3, V5 or V6. The V7 links were dropped because the study does not address large-model convergence or its causes; incompleteness across seeds is captured under V3 limits_scope. Channel-level inconsistency at low β does not challenge V3, which already allows individual units to differ, and full-space information stayed consistent. Results are qualitative figure descriptions with no numeric similarity values in the text. The models are small, low-dimensional latent-space models.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no test of convergence across models differing in architecture, objective, data, or modality as scale increases.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language models.
Tests probabilistic latent channels and full latent spaces in generative-model ensembles; it does not test neurons or whether individual units/bases match.

Does not test mapping one trained model's representations onto another's with little loss, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data. The deliberately optimized model-fusion example is not such a test.
Tests recurring information fragments in VAE/InfoGAN latent dimensions, not neurons, SAE features, or circuits generally.
Compares NMI and VI for channel similarity and reports variation across datasets and hyperparameters. It does not test out-of-distribution inputs or sweep similarity settings such as neighbour count.

Tests incomplete or variable channel-level consistency and variation in full-space consistency. It does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment, or whether alignment reflects a common model of reality.
